subject.title: [Feature]: Multi-role support in Chat UI for multi-agent workflows

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable per-message sender identity contract for multi-agent conversations, and which fields are canonical across protocol, transcripts, live/history payloads, and Control UI rendering?
rationale: The requested behavior crosses public Gateway schemas, session-state persistence, provenance/trust semantics, and UI identity rendering, and current senderLabel/provenance mechanisms are only partial hints that could drift if extended independently.

options.title: Design additive sender identity contract
options.body: Add a canonical sender object with stable id/kind/display/source metadata and route it through the protocol, persistence, events, and UI while preserving existing role and senderLabel compatibility.

options.title: Keep narrow partial fixes
options.body: Continue landing focused fixes like sessions_send prompt requester names and WebChat fallback labels without committing to a broad durable identity model yet.

options.title: Defer multi-agent UI identity
options.body: Leave this as a roadmap item until the broader multi-agent conversation and trust model is ready.

recommendation.title: Design additive sender identity contract
recommendation.body: Add a canonical sender object with stable id/kind/display/source metadata and route it through the protocol, persistence, events, and UI while preserving existing role and senderLabel compatibility.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the Gateway protocol and provenance surfaces that define the contract boundary for this feature.
